blocks.title: Observe
blocks.text: Von Neumann stores programs and their data in a common memory/address space, so instruction fetches and data transfers may contend for shared resources.

blocks.title: Explain
blocks.text: Harvard architecture separates instruction and data pathways, potentially allowing simultaneous instruction fetch and data access.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Modern systems often use unified main memory but separate instruction/data caches; the classification is a model of design trade-offs, not a universal speed ranking.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain the mechanism
blocks.text: Instruction and data transfers share memory/bus resources, so competing accesses can wait. Describe the shared resource and its effect, not claim all Von Neumann machines are slow.

questions.feedback: Von Neumann — Shared instruction/data memory organisation.
Harvard — Separate instruction/data stores or pathways.

blocks.title: Explain the mechanism
blocks.text: Harvard-style separation; fetch instruction and access data paths may operate in parallel. It differs from a single shared path even when control logic is the same CPU.
